```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_torch <- torch::torch_is_installed()
```

```{r setup}
library(graphlearnR)
```

Every model in graphlearnR consumes the same data structure, a `graph_data`
object. This article explains what it stores, the rules it enforces, and how
to get your data into it.

## The data model

A graph with `N` nodes and `E` stored edges has

| field | shape | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `N x F` matrix | node features |
| `edge_index` | `2 x E` integer matrix | row 1 source, row 2 target, 1-based |
| `y` | length `N` | node labels (factor or numeric) |
| `edge_attr` | `E x D` matrix | edge features |
| `edge_weight` | length `E` | scalar edge weights |
| `edge_y` | length `E` | edge labels |
| `graph_y` | length 1 | graph label |
| `train_mask`, `val_mask`, `test_mask` | length `N` logical | node splits |
| `node_ids` | length `N` | original identifiers |
| `edge_pair` | length `E` | pair id of each stored edge (undirected graphs) |

```{r}
g <- graph_data(
  x = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)),
  y = factor(c("a", "b", "a")),
  edge_weight = c(0.5, 2)
)
g
```

### Indexing is 1-based

Node `1` is the first row of `x`. Edge index matrices, seeds for sampling,
node pairs for link prediction, and every returned node id use the same
convention. The only place a 0-based index appears is at an explicit
boundary with other software, through `to_zero_based()` and
`from_zero_based()`.

```{r}
to_zero_based(g$edge_index)
```

### Direction

An edge `(i, j)` sends a message from `i` to `j`; layers aggregate over the
incoming edges of each node. A directed graph is stored as given.

For an undirected graph, give each pair once. graphlearnR stores both
directions next to each other and records the pair id. Edge level fields such
as weights are copied to both directions.

```{r}
u <- graph_data(edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)), edge_weight = c(1, 5),
                directed = FALSE)
u$edge_index
u$edge_weight
u$edge_pair
num_edges(u)
num_edges(u, unique_pairs = TRUE)
```

Giving both directions of an undirected pair is almost always a mistake, so
it raises a warning.

```{r}
w <- graph_data(edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 1)), directed = FALSE)
```

### Validation

`graph_data()` validates its input and fails with a message that names the
problem: out of range or fractional indices, missing values, mismatched
lengths, and overlapping masks.

```{r}
try(graph_data(edge_index = rbind(1, 5), num_nodes = 3))
try(graph_data(x = diag(2), train_mask = c(TRUE, FALSE), test_mask = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
```

`validate_graph()` runs the same checks on an object you have modified by
hand.

### Inspecting a graph

```{r}
k <- dataset_karate()
c(nodes = num_nodes(k), edges = num_edges(k), features = num_node_features(k))
has_self_loops(k)
has_isolated_nodes(k)
head(degree(k))
```

## Conversion

### From and to igraph

`from_igraph()` reads vertex names into `node_ids`, the `weight` edge
attribute into `edge_weight`, and any attributes you name into features.

```{r}
ig <- igraph::make_graph("Zachary")
igraph::V(ig)$age <- seq_len(igraph::vcount(ig))
gi <- from_igraph(ig, x_attrs = "age")
gi
back <- to_igraph(gi)
igraph::ecount(back)
```

An undirected igraph object becomes an undirected `graph_data`; the round
trip keeps the edge count.

### From an edge list

Real data rarely numbers nodes `1:N`. `graph_from_edgelist()` maps arbitrary
identifiers through an optional node table, which also supplies features and
labels. Nodes that appear in the table but in no edge are kept as isolated
nodes.

```{r}
edges <- data.frame(from = c("ann", "bob", "cat"), to = c("bob", "cat", "ann"),
                    strength = c(3, 1, 2))
nodes <- data.frame(id = c("ann", "bob", "cat", "dan"), age = c(31, 45, 27, 52),
                    group = c("x", "y", "x", "y"))
ge <- graph_from_edgelist(edges, nodes = nodes, feature_cols = "age",
                          label_col = "group", weight_col = "strength")
ge
ge$node_ids
edgelist_from_graph(ge)
```

### From an adjacency matrix

Dense and sparse (`Matrix`) adjacency matrices both work. A symmetric matrix
gives an undirected graph unless `directed = TRUE`. Entry `A[i, j]` is the
edge from `i` to `j`.

```{r}
A <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(1, 2, 3), j = c(2, 3, 1), x = c(1, 2, 3), dims = c(3, 3))
ga <- graph_from_adjacency(A)
ga$edge_index
adjacency_from_graph(ga)
```

### To tensors

`graph_tensors()` converts every field to a torch tensor on a chosen device:
features to floating point, indices and class labels to `long`, and masks to
`bool`. Indices stay 1-based, which is what R torch indexing expects.

```{r, eval = has_torch}
tt <- graph_tensors(k)
tt
tt$edge_index$dtype
```

## Many graphs: batching

Graph level tasks train on many small graphs. `graph_batch()` joins them into
one disconnected graph: node indices are offset so no edge crosses between
graphs, and `batch` records which graph each node belongs to.

```{r}
gs <- dataset_synthetic_graphs(3, seed = 1)
b <- graph_batch(gs)
b
b$node_ptr
table(b$batch)
```

`unbatch()` reverses the operation exactly.

```{r}
parts <- unbatch(b)
identical(parts[[2]]$edge_index, gs[[2]]$edge_index)
```

## Datasets

`graph_dataset()` wraps a list of graphs and applies an optional transform
when a graph is accessed. `write_graph_dataset()` and `graph_dataset_disk()`
keep large collections on disk, one file per graph, loading each on demand.

```{r}
ds <- graph_dataset(dataset_synthetic_graphs(20, seed = 2),
                    transform = add_degree_features)
ds
ncol(ds[[1]]$x)
```

Public benchmark datasets are downloaded, not bundled, and their MD5 checksum
is verified before use. `download_tu_dataset("MUTAG")` reads a TU Dortmund
graph classification dataset and `download_planetoid_raw("cora")` reads the
raw LINQS release of Cora; read their licenses before redistributing them.

## Transforms

Transforms are plain functions from a graph to a graph, so they compose with
`compose_transforms()` or with the native pipe.

```{r}
g2 <- graph_data(x = diag(3), edge_index = rbind(c(1, 1, 2), c(2, 2, 3)))
g2 |> coalesce_edges() |> add_self_loops() |> (\(h) h$edge_index)()
ks <- split_nodes(dataset_karate("degree"), seed = 1)
head(normalize_features(ks, stats_mask = ks$train_mask)$x)
```

Pass `stats_mask` to `normalize_features()` to compute centering and scaling
statistics from training nodes only, so test information does not leak into
the features.
